newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures erase early gains, end lower.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures erase early gains, end lower.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures erased early gains to end lower on Thursday as optimism over news that Nippon Credit Bank had agreed on a business alliance with Bankers Trust faded in the second session.
"When the market realised this was not the saviour of the banking sector, the market just turned around and went south," said a trader with a European futures house.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract ended 50 points below the technical support level of 17,600 against its previous close at 17,710.
Dealers said stop-loss sales were triggered around 17,600 and the contract succumbed to pressure despite strong buying interest from a large U.S. investment house.
"It did test the psychological level of 17,500. With this low close, the market's still looking bearish," said a trader with a local institution.
He said there was intermediate support for the June Nikkei around 17,300, but added, "The strength of the support is actually getting weaker until the 16,800-16,900 area."

But a trader with a Japanese futures house said he was not entirely bearish yet. "It was just a technical level that broke and so there was selling. But I wouldn't be surprised to see it bounce back to 18,000 tomorrow," he said.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 353.3 against its opening 356.5.
